exercises.title: Fibonacci with a memo
exercises.task: FibSlow recomputes the same values again and again. Fill the two holes of Fib so each value is computed once and remembered in memo. Run compares the number of calls.
hints: Before computing, look in the memo: if v, ok := memo[n]; ok { return v }.
After computing, store the result in memo[n], then return it.
The base case stays first: Fib(0) and Fib(1) need no memo.

exercises.title: Flatten a nested document
exercises.task: A nested document (as read from JSON) is a tree. Turn it into flat paths to its leaves: {"pos": {"line": 3}} becomes pos.line=3. Lists use their index: imports.0. The Run document is what a compiler might report about a Go file. A nested map is a smaller document: recursion.
hints: Write a helper walk(prefix string, v any, out map[string]string) and call it on each top-level key.
A type switch on v: map[string]any and []any recurse with a longer prefix; anything else is a leaf: out[prefix] = fmt.Sprint(v).
The new prefix is prefix + "." + key, except at the top level, where it is just key.
